metadata.case_name: Jamaica vs. Trinidad and Tobago (Caribbean institutional divergence)
metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Two Anglophone Caribbean democracies with SIMILAR founding P1 but DIFFERENT economic structure (Safeguard E: Trinidad's oil/gas rents cushion vs Jamaica's debt-and-crime trajectory): does similar P1 + different P4 produce divergent STABILITY STRESSES with NEITHER fragmenting? Pre-P1 gap (~0.087) sits inside the Mod4 ~0.10 margin -> near-tie, so the ordinal head-to-head is annotated as a Mod4 near-tie rather than a confident ranking. Decolonization footnote: the failed West Indies Federation as a fusion-prevention precedent.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record; both entities carry real MI v2 re-scores. 1962 independence (West Indies Federation collapse) -> 2024; scored ~1996 vs 2024. Caribbean (second case, with Haiti/DR case21) and the third decolonization case.

pre_event.event_description: Two former British West Indies colonies, both independent in 1962 after the West Indies Federation collapsed, enter the WGI era with similar institutional quality but sharply different economic structures: Trinidad and Tobago is a petro-state (oil and gas rents), while Jamaica is a tourism-and-remittance economy carrying a chronic debt overhang and a severe violent-crime problem.

Jamaica.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Jamaica: stable Westminster democracy with a heavy public-debt burden (long among the world's highest debt/GDP ratios) and one of the highest homicide rates in the hemisphere; low resource rents (P4 stress = debt + crime, not rentier capture).

Trinidad and Tobago.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Trinidad and Tobago: hydrocarbons (oil + LNG) supply substantial fiscal rents that cushion the economy; the Safeguard E test here is the MODERATE/positive pole (rents cushion, but expose the economy to commodity cycles and rising crime), not full rentier capture.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Trinidad and Tobago >= Jamaica by founding P1, but the gap (~0.087) sits INSIDE the Mod4 ~0.10 margin -> treat as a NEAR-TIE; do not assert a confident ordinal ranking. Both remain stable democracies; neither fragments.
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Pre-P1: Trinidad 0.614 vs Jamaica 0.527 (gap 0.087 < 0.10 margin) -> Mod4 near-tie. Similar P1, different P4 (Safeguard E rents vs debt/crime).
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Either state fragments, OR a clean, large divergence emerges that the near-tie reading cannot accommodate (i.e., the gap was real and ordinally decisive).

b_violence.prediction: Elevated CRIMINAL-violence risk (homicide), concentrated in Jamaica (and rising in Trinidad), but NOT state-fragmentation violence; no secession or civil war.
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Large-scale political/fragmentation violence or state breakdown in either state.

c_convergence.prediction: Modest DIVERGENCE in stability stresses driven by economic structure (Trinidad rent-cushioned, Jamaica debt-and-crime constrained), with neither fragmenting; MI gap roughly stable-to-widening.
c_convergence.basis: Similar founding P1 but different P4 should produce different stress profiles rather than convergence.
c_convergence.falsification_condition: Clear convergence of MI/outcomes, or one state fragments.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Jamaica's binding vulnerability is institutional/economic-structure (P1 + P2: debt service crowding out capacity, crime); Trinidad's is commodity-cycle exposure (P4). Neither produces collapse.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Failure driven by a different dimension, or actual state collapse.

e_fragment_count.prediction: 0 successor states for each; neither fragments.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: N/A -- not a democratic-transition reversal case; both are long-standing democracies.

Jamaica.outcome_summary: Stable democracy under chronic stress, no fragmentation. P1 essentially flat (0.527 -> 0.526) but MI fell 0.630 -> 0.571, dropping from Tier 2 to Tier 3 -- the debt-and-crime drag (P2/P4 erosion) showed up in the composite even as institutional quality held. Notable fiscal consolidation reduced the debt burden over the 2010s, but violent crime remained among the hemisphere's highest.
key_events: sustained IMF-anchored fiscal consolidation; debt/GDP reduced from extreme highs
persistently high homicide rate; periodic states of emergency

Trinidad and Tobago.outcome_summary: Rent-cushioned stability, no fragmentation. MI fell 0.672 -> 0.616 but held Tier 2; P1 declined 0.614 -> 0.492 as hydrocarbon dependence and rising crime weighed on governance scores. The rents cushioned aggregate outcomes (kept Tier 2) but exposed the economy to commodity cycles -- the moderate Safeguard E profile.
key_events: hydrocarbon revenue cushioned fiscal shocks; Heritage and Stabilisation Fund

a_trajectory.evidence: Pre-P1 order Trinidad (0.614) > Jamaica (0.527), gap 0.087; post-MI order Trinidad (0.616) > Jamaica (0.571), gap 0.045. Ordering held; both remained intact democracies.
a_trajectory.explanation: AUTO (Mod4): full pre-P1 gap 0.087 < margin 0.1 -> abstain (too close to call). | prior: AUTO (Mod4): full pre-P1 gap 0.087 < margin 0.1 -> abstain (too close to call). | prior: AUTO: full ordering matches: Trinidad and Tobago > Jamaica (by pre-P1) == outcome by post-MI; pre-P1 gap 0.087. MOD4 NEAR-TIE: gap 0.087 < 0.10 margin, so this is reported as a near-tie that happened to hold, NOT a confident ordinal ranking -- the prediction's near-tie framing is vindicated (both stable, no fragmentation

b_violence.evidence: Jamaica retained one of the hemisphere's highest homicide rates (periodic states of emergency); crime rose in Trinidad; no fragmentation violence in either.
b_violence.explanation: Elevated criminal-violence risk concentrated in Jamaica, with no state-fragmentation violence, exactly as predicted (Mod8).
b_violence.data_refreshed: 2026-06-28: focus=Jamaica pre-P1=0.527 -> LOW risk (MI v1, anchored)

c_convergence.evidence: MI-range 0.042 (pre) -> 0.045 (post): essentially flat. Clearer divergence appears in TIER (Jamaica 2 -> 3; Trinidad held 2) and in the structure of decline (Jamaica via debt/crime, Trinidad via P1/commodity exposure).
c_convergence.explanation: AUTO: outcome marginal DIVERGENCE (MI-range 0.042 -> 0.045). Direction (divergent stress profiles, neither fragmenting) is correct, but the raw MI-range barely moved, so the magnitude of the predicted divergence is weaker than 'clear' -> coded PARTIAL. The divergence is real but expressed mainly through the tier shift, not the MI gap.

d_failure_dimension.evidence: Jamaica's decline ran through economic structure / debt-and-crime (MI fell while P1 held flat); Trinidad's through P1 + commodity exposure.
d_failure_dimension.explanation: Divergent stress dimensions confirmed directionally. [STRICT RE-CODE per run6 §3(d): post-hoc 'primary dimension' identification invites confirmation bias; coded PARTIAL under strict standards.]
d_failure_dimension.computed_config: Jamaica: P4=0.79, P3=0.66, P5=0.60, P2=0.57, P1=0.53 | all pillars >= median -> no binding vulnerability (management-load/high-capacity case; relatively-lowest P1=0.53)

e_fragment_count.evidence: Zero successor states for each; neither fragmented.

analysis.overall_assessment: Directional confirmation with appropriate Mod4 discipline: a near-tie in founding P1 was reported as a near-tie, not a confident ranking, and both states stayed intact. Divergent economic structure (Safeguard E rents vs debt/crime) produced divergent stress profiles -- visible mainly in Jamaica's tier drop -- without fragmentation.
safeguards_triggered: E (resource rents -- moderate/positive pole, Trinidad and Tobago)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: When two democracies start from a near-tie in P1 (inside the Mod4 margin) but differ in economic structure, the framework correctly ABSTAINS on a confident ordinal ranking and instead predicts divergent STRESS PROFILES with neither fragmenting: Trinidad's hydrocarbon rents cushioned it into Tier 2 while Jamaica's debt-and-crime drag pulled it to Tier 3 -- divergence expressed through composition and tier, not through a widening headline gap.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; adds the second Caribbean case (with Haiti/DR case21), the third decolonization case, and a moderate Safeguard E exemplar plus a Mod4 near-tie discipline test.
analysis.strict_recode_note: Strict re-code applied per run6 (post-hoc d-dimension -> PARTIAL; near-tie a-trajectory annotated with Mod4). Honest aggregate target ~62-78%.
